correctness.rationale: Expanding each |psi_k><psi_k| and transposing the qubit produces exactly two positive singleton entries p0/2,p_{n−2}/2 and n−1 disjoint 2-by-2 real symmetric blocks B_k=(1/2)[[p_{k−1},−p_k],[−p_k,p_{k+1}]]. Each block has strictly positive trace and determinant (p_{k−1}p_{k+1}−p_k²)/4; thus the strict/equal/reversed local log-concavity cases give, respectively, one negative, one zero, or two positive eigenvalues. Summation establishes inertia (n+1+V,E,L), including n=2 and zero-extended endpoints. The binomial adjacent-ratio inequality is strict in the interior and the geometric progression has exactly n−3 zero blocks when n≥3. The known universal upper bound n−1 is reached exactly at all strict inequalities. Independent exact rational partial-transpose matrix construction and block determinant tests agree on 33 representative examples.

originality.rationale: The NPT maximal dimension result and negative-eigenvalue upper bound were established by Cubitt–Montanaro–Winter, Rana, and Johnston; they are not attributed to this work. What is new to our best knowledge is the complete exact sign/inertia classification within the natural diagonal mixture simplex, including necessity/sufficiency of local discrete log-concavity, binomial maximizing weights, and geometric zero-mode boundary. A generic block-diagonal proof is elementary once this specific state family is selected, but neither the general maximal count nor its attainment implies this entire weight-dependent classification.
residual_risks: An unindexed application of block-structured partial transposes might state the same log-concavity criterion.
The theorem concerns only diagonal mixtures of this nearest-neighbor family, not coherent mixtures.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural parametric classification of the inertia for mixtures in the standard nearest-neighbor maximal NPT-subspace family. Discrete curvature in experimentally meaningful mixture weights predicts the number of negative partial transpose eigenvalues and exact zero-mode transitions; the binomial family gives explicit high-dimensional extremizers. It is a motivated family-level structural invariant, not arbitrary tiny-spectrum calculation.

limitations: Positive weights; extension to zeros would create different block-boundary analysis.
Counts negative eigenvalues, not their absolute magnitudes or negativity.
